item.title: Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jackson 5 member Marlon Jackson says he has lived with prostate cancer for four years and has undergone surgery and radiation.
item.content:encoded:
Marlon Jackson has revealed he has stage 4 prostate cancer and says he has been living with cancer for four years.

The Jackson 5 singer disclosed his diagnosis in an interview on The Farah Shammas Podcast, where he told the host he was sharing news he had kept private.

“I’ve had cancer for four years,” Jackson told Shammas. When she asked what type of cancer he had, he answered, “Prostate, stage four.”

Jackson said he had his prostate removed and underwent radiation. He also said he kept up his regular walks, covering nearly four miles at a time about four times a week.

He talked about leaning on his faith through treatment and staying positive. Jackson said his doctor had told him he was doing better than initially expected.

After naming the stage of his cancer, Jackson offered reassurance: “I’m great. I’m good. Bad grass don’t die.”

The singer grew up in Gary, Indiana, and was still a child when he began performing with his brothers Jackie, Tito, Jermaine and Michael as The Jackson 5.

They recorded their first single for Steeltown Records before signing with Motown.

Their early Motown run made them the first group to top the Billboard Hot 100 with its first four singles. Those hits were “I Want You Back,” “ABC,” “The Love You Save” and “I’ll Be There.”

Marlon stayed with the group when the brothers left Motown and started recording as The Jacksons.

Motown retained the rights to the Jackson 5 name. The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inducted Marlon and his four brothers together in 1997, years before it inducted Michael as a solo artist.

Jackson has also been working on telling his family’s story. AllHipHop previously reported that he was tapped to narrate a documentary series about his father, Joe Jackson, who managed the brothers as they broke into the music business. The series was announced for BLK PRIME.

Jackson also thanked the people who supported him and prayed for him, telling Shammas he didn’t take their support for granted.

He said he stopped eating beef and pork in 1977 and cut out sugar after his cancer diagnosis.

item.title: NBA Vet Amar’e Stoudemire Trades His Jersey For A Police Uniform
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: NBA star Amar’e Stoudemire took an oath of public service as a police officer after a massive career in pro hoops.
item.content:encoded:
Amar’e Stoudemire went from wearing his name on a basketball jersey to putting on a Miami-Dade Schools Police Department uniform to help keep students and educators safe.

The former NBA star announced he had been sworn in as an officer, saying the job carries the trust of the community he will serve. The department welcomed him alongside Officer M. Larrinaga, whose appointment it announced in the same statement.

Stoudemire used the two uniforms to explain what the moment meant to him. He also thanked his family, instructors and classmates in BLE 401, giving them a place in an announcement that could have been all about the famous name on the badge.

“For 18 years, I wore a jersey with my name on the back. Today, I put on a uniform that carries the trust of my community.

I’m proud to have been sworn in as an officer with the Miami-Dade Schools Police Department. Being entrusted with the safety of our students, educators, and school communities is a responsibility I take to heart.

Baruch Hashem for the opportunity to serve. To my family, my instructors, and my BLE 401 classmates, thank you for being part of the journey.

Miami-Dade, it’s an honor to serve you.”

The department addressed its welcome to both officers. It described building relationships in school communities as part of the job, alongside keeping classrooms safe for the people who learn and work there.

“Today, the Miami-Dade Schools Police Department proudly welcomed our newest officers, Officer A. Stoudemire and Officer M. Larrinaga!

As they begin this new chapter in their law enforcement careers, they join a team dedicated to serving our school communities, building meaningful relationships, and ensuring a safe learning environment for every student and educator.

Please join us in congratulating our newest officers as they take on the responsibility and privilege of Protecting Our Future!

Welcome aboard, Officers Stoudemire and Larrinaga!”

In its announcement, the department introduced the former NBA star simply as Officer A. Stoudemire. His basketball career made the surname familiar. For the students and educators in Miami-Dade, the next association with that name will come from how he shows up for them.

item.title: Wale Spends A Day As Dunbar Principal While Students Study His Lyrics
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wale served as principal for a day at Washington's Dunbar High School, where students broke down his lyrics during Gifted Week.
item.content:encoded:
Wale spent a morning as principal at Washington, D.C.’s Paul Laurence Dunbar High School, where he made announcements, spoke to students and sat in on a lesson built around his own lyrics.

The November visit brought his third annual Gifted Week into a classroom at one of the city’s oldest public schools.

“Don’t get so caught up in what’s next that you forget to appreciate what’s in front of you,” Wale told students in NBC4 Washington’s report. He also urged them to stay focused and told them they were gifted.

The school is in Northwest Washington. The district traces Dunbar’s history to 1870 and identifies it as the country’s first public high school for Black students.

Wale has taken the principal-for-a-day role before.

He made a surprise appearance at the Duke Ellington School of the Arts during the previous year’s Gifted Week, when he also served as principal. This time, the high school visit was part of the program’s day devoted to the arts.

Wale and his management company, EQT, organized this year’s activities around the 15th anniversary of Ambition.

That album reached No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and produced “Lotus Flower Bomb,” his Grammy-nominated collaboration with Miguel, according to his former label.

Gifted Week had a sports media workshop scheduled for that evening at Howard University. The organizer billed it as a film panel with six executives who work in sports and music.

Wale arrived at the school with two new Grammy nominations. The Recording Academy nominated everything is a lot. for Best Rap Album and “Watching Us,” his song with Leon Thomas, for Best Melodic Rap Performance.

Gifted Week’s final day includes a Thanksgiving food drive and a sneaker-and-jersey design workshop.

item.title: Leaf Ward Plans A Return To The Studio After Federal Custody
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Leaf Ward talks fatherhood and recording again after federal custody, with Meek Mill and G Herbo calling in to welcome him.
item.content:encoded:
Leaf Ward is looking to get back in the studio after leaving federal custody.

The West Philadelphia rapper told Gillie Da King and Wallo on Million Dollaz Worth of Game that he wanted to record with other artists again.

Asked about getting back into rap, Ward said it wasn’t something he’d lost the ability to do. “That shit like riding a bike,” he said.

Meek Mill and G Herbo called on FaceTime, and Ward and Herbo talked about getting into the studio. Ward also talked about how becoming a father while locked up made him rethink his choices. He told the hosts how hard it was to miss his children’s birthdays and be unable to do anything for them that day.

Ward recalled looking back at old social media posts and questioning what he’d put out there.

“I could have been doing way better,” he said, looking back on the decisions he was making before prison.

Ward described coming home as feeling like “I got a second chance.” He credited men serving life sentences with changing how he saw his own situation. “They give you a different perspective,” he said.

The episode also put Ward back in front of a hometown audience that had followed his music well before the gun case. His earlier projects include solo records and collaborations with rappers outside Philadelphia.

Ward, whose legal name is Khalif Ward, was sentenced on January 23, 2025, to 46 months in federal prison.

He had pleaded guilty to possession of a machine gun and possession of a firearm by a felon, and Judge Joel H. Slomsky imposed a $25,000 fine.

Federal prosecutors traced the case to an August 2023 incident at a restaurant near the King of Prussia Mall.

AllHipHop covered the sentencing after the judge handed down the prison term.

By the time of that sentence, Ward had already put years into his catalog.

He released They Forgot: The Album in 2022, followed by Certified Member and Rated R in 2023. He also recorded “Risk Takers” with Millyz and Albee Al that year, one of the collaborations he had on the books before the case.

The three-year term of supervised release was part of the same federal sentence as the prison time.

item.title: Coco Jones Joins Queen Latifah In New Ice Age Movie
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Coco Jones will voice Peaches, the daughter of Queen Latifah's Ellie, in Disney's upcoming Ice Age: Boiling Point.
item.content:encoded:
Coco Jones is joining Queen Latifah in Ice Age: Boiling Point. Disney announced that Jones will voice Peaches, the daughter of Latifah’s Ellie and Ray Romano’s Manny.

It’s a return to Disney for Jones, who starred in the Disney Channel musical Let It Shine before building a career in R&B.

Jones takes over a role that Keke Palmer previously voiced in Ice Age: Continental Drift.

Disney also named Adam DeVine as Julian, Ashley Park as Zee and Josh Peck as Eddie in its new cast announcement.

John Leguizamo and Denis Leary are back as Sid and Diego, and Simon Pegg returns as Buck.

The film opens February 5, 2027.

It follows the herd into new parts of the Lost World, where Disney says they’ll encounter dinosaurs and lava. John C. Donkin, who directed The Ice Age Adventures of Buck Wild, directs this installment.

Lori Forte, who produced the original 2002 film, is back as a producer.

Jones was 14 when she played singer Roxie in Let It Shine.

The TV movie gave her a role built around music, with Tyler James Williams playing a young rapper who lets someone else take credit for his work.

Jones returned to television as Hilary Banks in Bel-Air, Peacock’s take on The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air.

Jones is also set to reprise the role and executive produce Hilary, a spinoff in development at Peacock. Peacock’s original series ran for four seasons.

In an interview with The Associated Press, she described how music and acting have worked together in her career.

“A very powerful way to be projected to the world is through TV and film as well as music,” Jones said.

Jones won the Grammy for Best R&B Performance for “ICU” in 2024 and released her debut album, Why Not More?, in 2025.

Latifah has played Ellie since Ice Age: The Meltdown. She’s also back in Grammy contention for the first time since 2008. Chris Wedge, who co-directed the original Ice Age, returns to voice Scrat.

In the new movie, Scrat also has a baby and a larger prehistoric counterpart named Jurassic Scrat.

item.title: GTA VI Pulls In $3.79 Billion On Day One
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: GTA VI opens with an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales after selling 32.5 million copies before launch.
item.content:encoded:
Grand Theft Auto VI pulled in an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales by the end of its first day.

Rockstar Games called it the biggest entertainment launch in history.

Rockstar put the figure in a statement filed by parent company Take-Two. The total reflects estimated retail sales worldwide through the end of November 19.

Rockstar separately counted 32.5 million copies sold before release, which it described as a preorder record across platforms.

The previous installment, Grand Theft Auto V, has shipped nearly 235 million copies over its lifetime, according to Rockstar. The new game’s opening figure measures dollars spent at retail rather than copies shipped.

Rockstar founder Sam Houser thanked players in the statement.

“We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you,” he said.

Playboi Carti, Don Toliver and Gunna have new tracks on the 34-song album Rockstar released with Atlantic Records.

The game has its own radio programming. On Vice City Rap Radio, JT and DJ Stevie J play records by Coi Leray and City Girls. Charlamagne tha God and Ivy Rivera host Early AF.

The game credits also list songs recorded for Real Dimez, a fictional Vice City rap duo.

Take A Daytrip produced “Money Don’t Lie,” which Derrick Milano co-wrote. Its soundtrack credits list Atlanta producer ATL Jacob among the producers on the duo’s “Vibin’ With The Dimez.”

Trick Daddy and Trina host Dirty South Classics, a station built around Southern rap.

AllHipHop’s guide to the game’s rap songs includes cuts by Outkast and Gangsta Boo. The separate Atlantic album is available on streaming, vinyl and CD.

item.title: Childish Gambino’s “This Is America” Hits 1 Billion YouTube Views
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Childish Gambino's "This Is America" is his first video to reach 1 billion YouTube views, eight years after its debut.
item.content:encoded:
Childish Gambino’s first music video has reached a billion YouTube views.

The official clip for “This Is America” was just over that mark in a November 21 snapshot from an independent YouTube tracker, more than eight years after Donald Glover released it.

The clip reached 110 million views in nine days, according to RCA Records. Glover introduced the song in May 2018 on the same night he hosted Saturday Night Live and served as its musical guest.

It debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, a first for Gambino, and stayed there for two weeks.

Director Hiro Murai and cinematographer Larkin Seiple shot it on 35mm inside a warehouse in South Gate, California.

Glover and a group of young dancers hold the center of the frame while violence and commotion break out behind them. Seiple said the crew originally tried moving the dancers in a circle, then decided to move the camera instead.

Seiple told American Cinematographer that the camera move let viewers stay with the dancers and spot other details as they entered the frame. The finished video uses six shots, including one in which the team gradually zoomed while circling the performers.

Choreographer Sherrie Silver pulled from both African and American dance, mixing South Africa’s gwara gwara with steps such as the Shoot.

“I was just trying to show that the kids are the light in all the darkness around them,” she told Glamour.

The Recording Academy awarded “This Is America” four Grammys in 2019: Record of the Year, Song of the Year, Best Rap/Sung Performance and Best Music Video.

item.title: GloRilla’s Basically Said Megan Thee Stallion Was Hating On Her Winning
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: GloRilla’s comments about one-sided support revives questions about her relationship with Megan Thee Stallion.
item.content:encoded:
GloRilla gave fans a reason to revisit those Megan Thee Stallion fallout rumors when a question about their relationship turned into a conversation about who roots for you when you’re winning. A fan asked Glo about Megan during her November 21 X Spaces, and this was her answer. 

“I love everybody and I want everybody to excel in what they do… sometimes people don’t feel the same way about you that you feel about them.”

That last part is why we’re here. Glo went on to say she was speaking generally about several people in her life. Still, Megan was the name in the question, so you can see why fans went straight back to the timeline.

Here’s some more:

“Sometimes people don’t feel the same way about you that you feel about them. I don’t conflict. I would say comes in when it’s time for it to be reciprocated. This is in general. This is a fruit. This is a ongoing thing with a few people in my life right now. people want to see you do good but they don’t wanna see you do (great).”

In 2024, these two had a good thing going. They teamed up on “Wanna Be,” brought in Cardi B for the remix and linked again on Megan’s “Accent.” Megan also brought Glo on the Hot Girl Summer Tour. If you caught that run, you can understand why people are asking what happened to the chemistry. 

The first big round of speculation came in May 2025. As AllHipHop reported at the time, Glo posted an Instagram Story featuring Tory Lanez’s “Y.D.L.R.” and took it down. Fans noticed that Megan appeared to have unfollowed her around the same time. Bloop.

Glo pushed back on the beef talk then, and Megan’s reason for the apparent unfollow remains unclear. By October, an online exchange involving Glo’s stylist EJ King and Megan’s hairstylist Kellon Deryck gave people another reason to reopen the case. Somewhere along the way, the beauty teams got all into it.

Then there’s the album theory. Glo’s Glorious opened with 69,000 equivalent album units, while MEGAN opened with 64,000. Megan’s album debuted at No. 3 and Glo’s at No. 5 in different chart weeks. Fans have treated those numbers like a motive. Neither artist has linked the sales to any tension between them. 

And now we have the “she was hating on my success” theory. Could it be D) All of the above?

Glo’s answer gets more interesting the longer you sit with it. She chose to talk about support going both ways. Megan’s side of that conversation is still missing. I think this will remain a mystery.

item.title: Philip Bailey Brings Comfort Cases Into Holiday Drive For Foster Youth
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Philip Bailey's Music Is Unity adds Comfort Cases to a holiday drive that supports foster youth and runs through December 4.
item.content:encoded:
Philip Bailey‘s Music Is Unity Foundation is raising money for foster youth in a new campaign that started November 16 and runs through December 4.

Music Is Unity, which Bailey started with his daughter Trinity in 2007, focuses on helping young people prepare to leave foster care and live on their own.

“Backstage Soundcheck is about more than music. It’s about exposure, inspiration, and helping young people envision new possibilities for their future,” Bailey told AllHipHop.com in a statement.

The Earth, Wind & Fire singer’s foundation says the fundraiser will support its own work as well as Rise Above, Kids in the Spotlight, Beyond Emancipation, Elevating Connections and a new partner, Comfort Cases.

Those organizations do different jobs.

Comfort Cases gives children backpacks filled with essentials when they enter foster care. The organization works with child welfare agencies to get items like pajamas, blankets and hygiene kits to kids who are just arriving.

Beyond Emancipation helps current and former foster youth with the transition to independent living, according to the foundation’s partner profiles, while Kids in the Spotlight gives young people a chance to write, cast and star in their own short films.

There’s a live show in the holiday campaign, too. Capital One Hall in Tysons, Virginia, and Oakland Ballet donated tickets so foster youth can see The Nutcracker through the foundation’s Backstage Soundcheck program.

The foundation also said each $50 donation earns one chance to win two tickets to the Rockettes’ Christmas Spectacular in New York on December 19.

That program usually shows young people what happens before concert doors open.

The foundation teamed with T.I. for July events in Brooklyn, Silver Spring and Charlotte, where it planned to introduce participants to behind-the-scenes work in live entertainment.

At past tour stops, the program has included time for participants to ask Bailey and the touring crew questions.

Music Is Unity had already announced it was working with Comfort Cases alongside its July Backstage Soundcheck dates.

Philip Bailey performing with Earth, Wind & Fire (file photo). Photo: Craig ONeal, CC BY 2.0. Cropped.

item.title: Sir Mix-A-Lot Gets A Lasting Spot In Seattle Music Exhibition
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Sir Mix-A-Lot gets a lasting section at Seattle's Museum of Pop Culture, with Stas THEE Boss playing the opening day.
item.content:encoded:
Sir Mix-A-Lot is getting a lasting spot in a new Seattle museum exhibition that puts Hip-Hop alongside the other sounds the region sent out into the world.

The Museum of Pop Culture opened Puget Sound Stories: Seattle Music + Beyond on November 21, with a section on the rapper.

Chief Collections and Exhibitions Officer Jacob McMurray told the museum that some artists will stay in the galleries as other stories rotate in.

“The idea is to always have sections on those mainstream stories, such as grunge or Sir Mix-A-Lot or Heart,” he said in an interview.

The exhibition starts with 25 stories from different parts of the region’s music history.

A companion exhibition about Jimi Hendrix’s Seattle roots opens the same day, with Janie Hendrix scheduled for a Q&A.

McMurray said the museum expects to rotate in two or three sections about lesser-known musicians and scenes each year.

Visitors can suggest what to cover next, and the museum plans to keep adding to a video area that starts with about 30 short pieces, including performances and oral histories.

Sir Mix-A-Lot’s section looks at how his records carried Seattle Hip-Hop beyond the Northwest. “Posse on Broadway” put a Seattle street in the title, and “Baby Got Back” earned him the Grammy for Best Rap Solo Performance in 1993.

Stas THEE Boss gets space in the exhibition as well as time on the stage. She was one half of THEESatisfaction, the Seattle duo that recorded for Sub Pop and brought rap, jazz and soul together.

Her KEXP biography traces her from Tacoma’s Hilltop to Seattle’s South End and through her work as a rapper, producer and DJ. She went on to host Street Sounds, KEXP’s long-running Hip-Hop mix show.
